summary:
Project Summary — MINATO AMAMIYA: Astro TRAINER 

MINATO AMAMIYA: Astro TRAINER is an interactive digital learning experience designed to make space exploration more accessible, engaging and understandable for learners worldwide. Developed in response to NASA Space Apps Challenge's Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge, the project transforms space education into an immersive, game-based experience where users can explore astronaut-related concepts, engage with space missions and develop scientific curiosity through interactive learning.

Rather than limiting space education to textbooks and theoretical explanations, Astro Trainer aims to bring learners closer to the realities of space exploration through an engaging environment that combines learning, exploration and problem-solving. It encourages users to understand the science behind space missions while making complex concepts more approachable.

The project addresses the need for accessible and engaging space education, particularly for young learners who may have limited opportunities to experience space-related learning beyond conventional classroom resources. By combining educational value with interactive digital engagement, Astro Trainer seeks to inspire curiosity, strengthen scientific awareness and encourage the next generation to explore the possibilities of space science.
details: MINATO AMAMIYA – Astro Trainer Developed by ASTRAK – Kiyoka's Unit Created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, MINATO AMAMIYA – Astro Trainer is a browser-based interactive game developed in response to the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. It introduces players to the complexities of human space exploration through multiple astronaut-training missions, combining scientific learning with interactive decision-making. The game features a range of space-related activities and scientifically researched scenarios, including solar radiation, Martian dust storms, micrometeoroid impacts, delayed resupply and water-ice discoveries. Each scenario presents players with a mission situation in which they must investigate the circumstances, evaluate available options and make decisions that influence the outpost and its resources. Through this approach, players engage with the challenges of space exploration while developing critical thinking, problem-solving and resource-management skills. Our project aims to make space science more engaging and accessible, particularly for young learners. By transforming scientific concepts into interactive missions, it encourages curiosity, exploration and a better understanding of the challenges astronauts may encounter beyond Earth. The project was developed using HTML, CSS and Java, with Cloudflare and GitHub supporting the development process and other project-related uses. Astro Trainer aspires to make learning about space a more interactive, educational and globally accessible experience, encouraging the next generation to take an interest in space science and exploration.
